title: I Who Have Never Known Men
author: Jacqueline Harpman
review:
2.5/5 What the hell was that? I'm confused why this is so popular, it doesn't really go anywhere. There were a few good plot moments but I really expected more. I didn't connect with any of the characters, and the themes are just okay.

Feel like I'd rather have read something by Octavia Butler or Ursula K Le Guin, they have a similarly bleak style but typically have better plot progression. This is just depressing and bleak and I don't really take anything away from it.

Feels a bit pointless overall, definitely a tedious hyper-detailed survival story that is often very boring. The writing is solid but nothing extraordinary. The core mystery is interesting but the lack of answers is really unsatisfying and the ending is lame as hell.

Maybe I didn't get it, not sure. I'll be looking up some discussions on this to see if I'm missing something deeper than what I took away from it. I don't recommend reading this to be honest.

highlights.text: I felt a surge of grief, I, who had never known men, as I stood in front of this man who had wanted to overcome fear and despair to enter eternity upright and furious.

I will only be truly dead if nobody ever comes, if the centuries, then the millennia go by for so long that this planet, which I no longer believe is Earth, no longer exists. As long as the sheets of paper covered in my handwriting lie on this table, I can become a reality in someone’s mind. Then everything will be obliterated, the suns will burn out and I will disappear like the universe.
